Halo 2 testing begins today on PC for Insiders

I was sent a flight test key so I gave it a try. About half of the campaign is playable in this test so I went through that. Visually it's competent enough, but the artists took quite a lot of liberty to change textures and looks of levels, so some of these changes won't appeal to every one. The new graphics also make a lot of indoor areas much darker as well. Maybe if they improved the lighting in this game to have some bounce lighting it won't be so bad. The stuttering from the rest of the master chief collection still remains. I.e. if you're playing on a high refresh rate display and you've unlocked the frames, it'll look jittery due to animations and other things being locked to 60fps. And the game is quite unstable probably due to it still being a work in progress. I get frame drops in areas when using the updated graphics, even though visually it doesn't look good enough to cause such a performance degradation (runs fine when I switch to the original graphics at least). The game is very unstable though as it crashes during loading if I play at 4k. I still experienced crashes when I changed it to 1080p, but they were more rare. I think it has something to do with video memory leaks. Pretty bad considering that this is a port of an xbox 360 game that runs out of VRAM on an 8GB GPU during loading. Also, the prerendered cutscenes are cool, but good lord, sjw designs strike again as they turned Miranda Keyes into an ugly woman. She's supposed to be in her late 20s but she looks almost 2 decades older. But at least Cortana looks fine, so that's nice I guess...

Audio wise it seems to be better compared to Reach on PC. I didn't notice any weird volume bugs or lacking sound effects. Some of the new sound effects are better, while others I found to be weaker (e.g. the sound of equipping the energy sword sounds much weaker in the new version). The redone music is also pretty good for the most part, however for one of the licensed songs they used something completely different (but the original is still there if you switch to the original game version). I wish they did additional subtitle work as the cutscenes will have them but not in game dialogue. And with some of the audio mixing it becomes a bit difficult to understand what some of the characters are saying.

I only tried one round of multiplayer. I never had an original xbox so I have no idea what the original's multiplayer is like, so I can't really compare. I think right now xbox players have a huge advantage because they have aim assist on consoles, but not on PC, which is kind of a bummer. As for co-op, like the other Halo PC games there's no local co-op, which is expected but still a big letdown. It's shameful that a multibillion dollar company can't be arsed to add in something the console versions already had 15 years ago to the PC versions of the #1 game that put their console on the map. In terms of options, the graphics settings are extremely basic. Pretty much like Reach and Halo 1 on PC (3 graphics presets with options to toggle vsync, change resolution, fov sliders, framerate lock).

Overall it's an OK port. It's technically lacking, some of the audiovisual changes may not be for everyone, but at least you can toggle them on the fly with the press of a button. And unlike the atrocity that is the FF7 "remake," at least Halo 2 MCC is a proper remake (i.e. same story beats, no change to dialogue, weapon designs, difficulty, etc).
